lessons.name: no state's predicate is the diagonal one: for any states at all and any map f from states to predicates on states, the predicate i ↦ ¬ f i i differs from f j at j itself — Cantor's diagonal in Lawvere's form (Lawvere 1969, doi 10.1007/BFb0080769)
lessons.why: the i-th entry of a row, false past the end; written out because List.getD reaches propext -/ def bit : List Bool → Nat → Bool | [], _ => false | x :: _, 0 => x | _ :: xs, n + 1 => bit xs n /-- the i-th row of a table, empty past the end -/ def rowAt : List (List Bool) → Nat → List Bool | [], _ => [] | x :: _, 0 => x | _ :: xs, n + 1 => rowAt xs n /-- every row of n booleans -/ def rows : Nat → List (List Bool) | 0 => [[]] | n + 1 => (rows n).flatMap (fun r => [false :: r, true :: r]) /-- every table of k rows drawn from rs -/ def tablesOf (rs : List (List Bool)) : Nat → List (List (List Bool)) | 0 => [[]] | k + 1 => (tablesOf rs k).flatMap (fun t => rs.map (fun r => r :: t)) /-- every self-model of n states: row i is the predicate state i assigns to every state -/ def models (n : Nat) : List (List (List Bool)) := tablesOf (rows n) n /-- the diagonal predicate: state i holds of itself exactly when its own row says it does not -/ def diag (t : List (List Bool)) : List Bool := (List.range t.length).map (fun i => !(bit (rowAt t i) i)) /-- no state's predicate is the diagonal one: for any states at all and any map f from states to predicates on states, the predicate i ↦ ¬ f i i differs from f j at j itself — Cantor's diagonal in Lawvere's form (Lawvere 1969, doi 10.1007/BFb0080769)
lessons.statement: ∀ {α : Type} (f : α → α → Bool) (j : α), (fun i => !(f i i)) ≠ f j

lessons.name: so no system's states map onto all predicates on its states: a complete self-model would have to represent the diagonal, and the diagonal escapes every state — there is no complete self-model (Lawvere 1969, doi 10.1007/BFb0080769). Self-reference itself is not refused: Kleene's recursion theorem builds programs that print their own text (Kleene 1938, doi 10.2307/2267778), proved mathematics this wing cites and does not seal
lessons.statement: ∀ {α : Type}, ¬ ∃ e : α → α → Bool, ∀ p : α → Bool, ∃ a, e a = p

lessons.name: checked over every self-model of the 3 corners of the affect trinity (feeling, thought, emotion): in all 512 tables the diagonal predicate is no row of the table
lessons.statement: (models 3).all (fun t => t.all (fun r => r != diag t)) = true ∧ (models 3).length = 512

lessons.name: negation on Bool fixes neither value — Lawvere's corollary: an onto self-model would give every map on Bool a fixed point, and this one has none
